title: JMoney Does the Math, Philly Pays the Price: Jeanty Heads to Team Pillbert in a Three-for-One
dek: Alan gets the workhorse running back he wanted and watches his title odds drop five points, while Jordan collects a trio of pass catchers whose points add up to exactly 0.4 more than what he gave away.
body: The first big trade of the 2026 season landed before Week 5, and it came from two very different corners of the Buckaroo Football League. Counting or not Counting GV (Jordan) shipped running back Ashton Jeanty to Team Pillbert (Alan). In return Jordan got three players: tight end Isaiah Likely and wide receivers Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston. It's a classic consolidation deal, with the league villain trading a stack of pieces for one big name.

Start with what Philly got, because it's the headliner. Jeanty had 64.4 points through four weeks before the trade, about 16.1 a week, and he did it all by himself. Nobody else in this deal comes close on a per-week basis. If Alan's plan was to grab the best player in the trade and dare everyone to stop him, he got the right guy.

Now look at Jordan's side, and you can almost picture JMoney with a calculator. Likely brought 18.2 points over three weeks on a roster, Egbuka brought 28.6 over four, and Boston brought 18 in just two weeks of being owned. That adds up to 64.8 points, which is 0.4 more than Jeanty's 64.4. The man who's here for the numbers made the numbers match almost exactly, and then came out slightly ahead. Whether three roster spots' worth of production beats one star's production is a question for the football people. On the spreadsheet, it's a dead heat with a rounding error in Jordan's favor.

Then there are the title odds, and they tell a different story than the hype. Team Pillbert went into the deal at 20% to win the Buckaroo Bowl and came out at 15%. That's a five-point drop for the team that landed the best player in the trade. Counting or not Counting GV sat at 0% before and is still at 0% after, so the trade didn't save JMoney's season, but it didn't hurt it either. The projections seem to think Alan gave up too much depth to get his star.

So who won on paper? By the title odds, it's Jordan, mostly because he was the only one who didn't lose anything. Alan paid three players and five percentage points of championship equity for one running back, and in this league, watching the villain overpay is its own kind of victory. Jeanty can still make the models look silly over the next few weeks. Until he does, the scoreboard says the band kid out-negotiated the bad guy.

social.author: Spreadsheet Sammy
social.text: JMoney gave up 64.4 points and got back 64.8. Three players, a 0.4-point profit, and zero emotional attachment. That's not a trade, that's an audit.

social.author: Pillbert Truthers
social.text: Philly said 'give me the best player in the deal' and walked out with Jeanty. The models can drop us to 15% all they want. Villains don't read projections.

social.author: Buckaroo Odds Desk
social.text: Title odds after the Jeanty deal: Team Pillbert 20% to 15%. Counting or not Counting GV 0% to 0%. Only one team lost ground here, and it's the one that got the star.

social.author: Waiver Wire Whisperer
social.text: Denzel Boston had been on a roster for two weeks and is already a trade chip in a deal for Ashton Jeanty. Quickest promotion in league history.

social.author: Cheesehead Correspondent
social.text: Somewhere Alan is telling everyone he fleeced JMoney, while the odds board quietly took five points off his title chances. Love that for the league.
